title: Mastering Ocular Alignment: From Krimsky to Maddox
summary: A comprehensive guide to motor and sensory strabismus examination techniques. This poster details the gold-standard Prism Cover Test, corneal reflex methods, and subjective dissociation tests used by fellowship-trained pediatric ophthalmologists and strabismologists.

sections.title: The Gold Standard: Prism Cover Test (PCT)
content: Step 1: Ensure patient has adequate visual acuity for fixation (ideally 6/60 or better).
Step 2: Perform Cover-Uncover test to differentiate Tropia (manifest) from Phoria (latent).
Step 3: Perform Alternate Cover Test (ACT) to dissociate the eyes and reveal total deviation.
Step 4: Introduce prisms over one eye (usually non-fixing) until all movement is neutralized.
Step 5: Over-correct slightly and then reduce to find the exact neutralization point.

sections.title: Maddox Rod: Subjective Dissociation
content: Optical Principle: High-powered cylinders convert a point source of light into a streak.
Orientation: The streak is perceived 90 degrees to the axis of the cylinders.
Horizontal Deviation: Rods horizontal -> Vertical streak (measures Esophoria/Exophoria).
Vertical Deviation: Rods vertical -> Horizontal streak (measures Hyperphoria).
Cyclodeviation: Use two Maddox rods (Double Maddox Rod test) to measure degrees of torsion.

sections.title: Maddox Wing: Near Measurement
content: Fixed Distance: Measured specifically at 33 cm (near).
Dissociation: Septum separates the two eyes visually.
Right Eye Sees: White arrow (horizontal) and Red arrow (vertical).
Left Eye Sees: Horizontal scale (numbers) and Vertical scale (numbers).
Measurement: Patient reports where the arrow points on the numbered scale.
Torsion: Includes a small adjustable lever for measuring cyclodeviation.

sections.title: Head-to-Head: Maddox Rod vs. Maddox Wing
Critical Prism Rules & Orientation
content: Prism Orientation: Glass prisms MUST be held in the position of minimum deviation.
Plastic/Fresnel Prisms: Must be held in the Frontal Plane (Preston's position).
Apex vs. Base: Prisms always shift the image towards the APEX; Base goes opposite to the deviation.
Stacking Prisms: Do not stack two prisms of the same direction in one eye; additive error occurs.
Oblique Deviations: Do not tilt the prism; use two separate prisms for vertical and horizontal.

content.explanation: Maddox Rod: Horizontal cylinders = Vertical streak (Horizontal dev). Vertical cylinders = Horizontal streak (Vertical dev).

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Protocol
content: 1. Hirschberg (Screening for gross deviation)
2. Cover-Uncover (Determine manifest vs latent)
3. Alternate Cover Test (Measure total deviation with PCT)
4. Extraocular Motility (Check for underactions/overactions)
5. Sensory Testing (Worth 4-Dot, Bagolini, Stereoacuity)
6. Cycloplegic Refraction (Essential for Accommodative Esotropia)

sections.title: Landmark Concept: Prism Adaptation Test (PAT)
sections.content: The Prism Adaptation Test (PAT) involves wearing prisms for hours or days to evaluate for 'prism adaptation' or 'eating the prism.' In the landmark PAT study, patients with acquired esotropia who responded to prisms with further deviation required larger surgical dosages for successful outcomes.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & Pitfalls
content: Bielschowsky Head Tilt Test: Mandatory for identifying the paretic muscle in vertical deviations (Superior Oblique palsy).
Monocular vs. Binocular: PCT is a binocular test; Hirschberg/Krimsky are technically binocular but used when binocularity is disrupted.
Prism Diopter (PD) vs. Degrees: 1 Degree ≈ 2 Prism Diopters.
Suppression: If a patient suppresses, Maddox Rod will only show one image; the test becomes invalid.
Latent Nystagmus: Use a high plus lens (e.g., +10.00D) instead of an opaque occluder to prevent inducing nystagmus during PCT.

sections.title: Emergency Red Flags
content: Sudden Onset Diplopia: Rule out 3rd, 4th, or 6th Nerve Palsy.
Varying Deviation: Rule out Myasthenia Gravis (check for ptosis/fatigue).
New Onset Esotropia: Rule out intracranial pressure elevation (CN VI palsy).
Strabismus with Leukocoria: MUST rule out Retinoblastoma via dilated fundus exam.
Pupil Involving 3rd Nerve Palsy: Emergency! Neuro-imaging for Aneurysm.
